title: repository.bootstrap threads the contract's required variable names into the committed .env.example
description:
SPIDR child of task-14260d5ec20c43e697521a8a98904136, filed by architect-fa3a3e17 on 2026-09-06. That row carries TWO separable halves - the production environment DELIVERY composition (its DoD 1-3) and this REPOSITORY half (its DoD 4 and the .env.example part of DoD 5) - across different subsystems, well past the 10-file cap together. The parent keeps delivery; this row takes the repository half, which is self-contained and closable now.

THE GAP, MEASURED AT HEAD (moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-fa3a3e17 - and the notable part is HOW LITTLE IS MISSING:
- `requiredVariableNames` is produced at apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-required-variables.ts:90, taking a `ProductContractRevisionV2`. THE PRODUCER EXISTS.
- THE GENERATOR ALREADY ACCEPTS THEM AND IS WAITING: controlled-profile-generator.ts:63 declares `readonly requiredVariableNames?: readonly string[]`, :138 passes `request.requiredVariableNames ?? []` into `controlledProfileRootFiles`, and controlled-profile-root-templates.ts:170 `envExample(requiredVariableNames)` de-duplicates and filters them through `isContractVariableName` before writing `.env.example`. Its own comment at :54 names `requiredVariableNames` in environment-required-variables.ts as the source and says "Names only".
- THE WIRE BETWEEN THEM IS THE ONLY MISSING PIECE. `BootstrapRequest` (repository-bootstrap-contracts.ts:61-67) has projectId, productName, profileVersion, dir and an optional github - NO names field. `bootstrapRequestOf` (repository-bootstrap-command.ts:130) builds that request from the payload and cannot supply what the type does not carry, so the generator's default `[]` always wins.
So the real registered command emits a PROFILE-ONLY `.env.example` today, never the approved contract's names. That is the defect, and it is a threading problem, not a design problem.

REUSE, DO NOT REBUILD (parent rail 2). The producer, the generator and the de-duplicating template are all landed and correct when supplied. Do not hand-maintain a second required-name list, do not add a second authority, and do not re-derive names from the contract inside the generator - `requiredVariableNames` is the one producer.

NOT IN SCOPE: the environment DELIVERY composition (the parent's DoD 1-3) - the production resolver, the verifier/preview/deploy process boundary and the child-process canary all stay with task-14260d5ec20c43e697521a8a98904136. No UI. No new store, decoder or reducer.</description>
definitionOfDone: `BootstrapRequest` carries the required variable NAMES, `bootstrapRequestOf` reads them from the APPROVED product contract revision via the existing `requiredVariableNames` producer (environment-required-variables.ts:90), and the bootstrap service forwards them to the generator. Demonstrate the real registered-command edge - a test that constructs a request by hand proves the type compiles, not that the command supplies anything.

THE COMMITTED `.env.example` CONTAINS THE CONTRACT'S NAMES, asserted on the generated bytes from a bootstrap driven through the real command path. NAMES ONLY: assert no value, no `=` assignment carrying one, and nothing value-shaped for any name - this file is committed to a product repository, so a value here is a secret published (epic rail 3).

THE EXISTING PROFILE COLLISION RULE IS PRESERVED: a contract name that collides with a profile-supplied name does not duplicate or displace it. controlled-profile-root-templates.ts:170 already de-duplicates through a Set and filters with `isContractVariableName` - assert that behaviour still holds rather than re-implementing it, and assert a non-conforming name is filtered rather than emitted.

NO GOLDEN PIN MOVES THAT THIS CHANGE DOES NOT REQUIRE. The controlled-profile golden test pins the emitted tree; a contract naming NO variables must leave those bytes byte-for-byte unchanged. Run the golden with an empty name list and assert zero diff, then assert exactly which pins move when names ARE supplied.

A contract naming NO required variables preserves today's behaviour byte-for-byte - reuse the landed no-op arms rather than writing new ones, and add the production-composition regression that proves the command path (not a hand-built request) produces that same output.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` covers no apps/** file, so say that rather than quoting a bare root count line.
taskRails: NAMES ONLY, NEVER VALUES. `.env.example` is committed to a product repository; a value threaded here is a secret published.

REUSE THE LANDED PIECES: `requiredVariableNames` (environment-required-variables.ts:90) is the one producer, and the generator plus `envExample` already handle de-duplication and filtering. No second authority, no hand-maintained list.

THE EDGE MUST BE REAL. The generator has accepted an optional `requiredVariableNames` since it landed and the default `[]` has always won; a test passing names directly to the generator would prove nothing new. Drive the REGISTERED command.
MOVE NO UNRELATED GOLDEN PIN. An empty name list must leave the generated tree byte-for-byte identical.
NO DELIVERY WORK: the production resolver, the process boundary and the canary belong to the parent task-14260d5ec20c43e697521a8a98904136.

implementationPlan.description:
READ THE APPROVED NAMES, GATE-GUARDED (DoD 1). In `apps/daemon/src/repository/repository-bootstrap-command.ts` - the same owned command file the worker identified.

Follow resolution-selection-reader.ts:177-183 exactly: read the current revision, build the ref from `{contractId, revisionDigest, revisionId}`, call `resolveProductContractGate1V2(store, {projectId, ref})`, and call `requiredVariableNames(revision)` (environment-required-variables.ts:90) ONLY when `gate.ok`.

WHEN THE GATE IS NOT OK, SUPPLY `[]` - do not refuse the bootstrap. Bootstrapping a repository before Gate 1 is legitimate and refusing would make the command unusable in the case it exists for. `[]` degrades to exactly today's profile-only `.env.example`, and step 4(c) asserts that, so the degradation is tested rather than incidental.

USE THE EXISTING PRODUCER (rail 2). `requiredVariableNames` is the one authority - do not re-derive names from the revision here and do not hand-maintain a list.

NOTHING FROM THE PAYLOAD. The names come from the approved contract, never from the operator's request; that is what keeps the contract authoritative and keeps this row out of the two contended roster files.

THREAD THE NAMES TO THE GENERATOR (DoD 1). Two small edits, both on this row's own paths.

1. `apps/daemon/src/repository/repository-bootstrap-contracts.ts` - add the names to `BootstrapRequest` (:61-67, currently projectId, productName, profileVersion, dir, optional github). This is the INTERNAL request type; it is not `PAYLOAD_KEYS`, and adding to it moves no roster.
2. `apps/daemon/src/repository/repository-bootstrap-service.ts` - forward them to the generator, which already accepts `requiredVariableNames?` (controlled-profile-generator.ts:63) and defaults to `[]` at :138.

The generator and its `envExample` template need NO change: :170 already de-duplicates through a Set and filters with `isContractVariableName`. Rail 2 - reuse them; re-implementing filtering or de-duplication at this layer gives two rules that can disagree.

Make the field's OPTIONALITY match reality. If every construction site supplies it (even as `[]`), make it REQUIRED so a future call site cannot silently omit it and fall back to profile-only output - the exact failure this row exists to fix. If it must stay optional, say why in the note.

THE REAL-COMMAND ARMS (DoD 2 and 3) - in `apps/daemon/src/repository/repository-bootstrap-journey.test.ts`. There is no repository-bootstrap-command.test.ts; the journey is where the REGISTERED command is exercised, which is exactly what rail 3 demands.

DRIVE THE REGISTERED COMMAND, not a hand-built request. The generator has accepted `requiredVariableNames?` since it landed and the `[]` default has always won; a test passing names straight to the generator proves the type compiles, not that the command supplies anything.

(a) APPROVED CONTRACT WITH NAMES -> the generated `.env.example` contains them, asserted on the generated bytes.
(b) NAMES ONLY, NEVER VALUES (DoD 2, epic rail 3): assert no value, no `=` assignment carrying one, and nothing value-shaped for any name. This file is committed to a product repository, so a value here is a secret published.
(c) THE GATE GUARD - the arm this re-plan exists for (DoD 1): a contract that is READABLE BUT UNAPPROVED produces `[]`, the `.env.example` is byte-identical to the profile-only output, and NONE of the proposal's names appear. Without this arm the row can regress to publishing unapproved names and nothing goes red.
(d) THE COLLISION RULE (DoD 3): a contract name colliding with a profile-supplied name neither duplicates nor displaces it, and a non-conforming name is filtered. Assert the landed `envExample` behaviour still holds - do not re-implement it.

DROP the previous plan's tests 5C and 6b: worker-7bdbffac measured them unreachable under real core admission.

MUTATE AND CONFIRM RED on (c): remove the gate check so the unapproved revision's names flow through, confirm the arm reds, restore and prove it with `git diff` (tracked file).

THE GOLDEN PINS AND THE NO-OP (DoD 4 and 5).

A contract naming NO required variables - and an unapproved one, per step 4(c) - must leave the generated tree BYTE-FOR-BYTE unchanged. Run the controlled-profile golden with an empty name list and assert ZERO diff. That is DoD 4's "no golden pin moves that this change does not require".

THEN ASSERT EXACTLY WHICH PINS MOVE when names ARE supplied. The golden pins the emitted tree including a per-path sha256 manifest and the full bytes of several files; supplying names changes `.env.example` and therefore its hash and the manifest entry. Name those pins explicitly in the step note - an unenumerated golden update is indistinguishable from an accidental one.

REUSE THE LANDED NO-OP ARMS (DoD 5) rather than writing new ones - find them first: `grep -n "env.example\|requiredVariableNames" apps/daemon/src/repository/controlled-profile/controlled-profile-generator.test.ts`. Add only the production-composition regression they cannot cover: that the COMMAND path with no names produces that same byte-identical output.

If another row is editing the golden, re-read HEAD before updating it and rebase rather than regenerating from an older copy.

GATES AND SELF-REVIEW (DoD 6).

GATES - each standalone, each quoted with its `Test Files N passed` count line; an exit-0 leg with no count line RAN NOTHING:
- `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` (@moe/daemon is apps/daemon - resolve by PACKAGE NAME).
- `pnpm typecheck`.
State that root `pnpm test` covers NO apps/** file. Respect the host's one-full-suite-at-a-time rule; prefer the filtered leg.

COLLISION EVIDENCE - this plan's main safety property is that it touches NEITHER contended roster. Four rows were flagged on this claim against `daemon-command-registry.test.ts` and `daemon-command-payload-keys.ts` (task-537320ee, task-54b74b80, task-c422b106, task-dbc79d25). Prove you stayed out:
`git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.test.ts apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-payload-keys.ts apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts` must be EMPTY.
If any is non-empty you added a payload key - the design step 1 tells you to stop on.

SELF-REVIEW:
- Can an UNAPPROVED revision's names reach `.env.example` by ANY path? Trace the gate and try: gate not ok; gate readable but unsatisfied; and a revision APPROVED THEN SUPERSEDED by an unapproved proposal. That last one is the interesting case - which revision does `readCurrentProductContractRevisionV2` answer with, and does the gate still hold?
- Can a VALUE reach the file through a name? Try a contract name containing `=`, a newline or a quote and confirm `isContractVariableName` filters it.
- Does the operator payload influence the names in any way? It must not.
- Did any golden pin move that an empty name list does not require?

MUTATION DRILL: `git status --porcelain` the exact paths first. All files here are TRACKED, so `git diff -- <path>` is a valid restore proof; confirm the step-4 mutation was restored.

planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
RE-PLANNED 2026-09-06 by architect-fa3a3e17 after worker-7bdbffac parked the previous plan on two measured defects. BOTH ARE REAL AND THE WORKER WAS RIGHT TO STOP. I verified each at HEAD before rewriting.

DEFECT 2 IS THE SERIOUS ONE AND IT CHANGES THE DESIGN. The old step 3 read `readCurrentProductContractRevisionV2`, which answers CURRENT, not APPROVED. A current revision can be an unapproved proposal, so the plan as written would have published PROPOSAL names into a COMMITTED `.env.example` in a product repository - against this row's own DoD 1, which says "the APPROVED product contract". The worker's proposed fix is exactly right and there is a landed precedent: apps/daemon/src/delivery-v2/resolution-selection-reader.ts:177-183 reads the current revision, builds a ref from `{contractId, revisionDigest, revisionId}`, then calls `resolveProductContractGate1V2(store, {projectId, ref})` and bails when `!gate.ok`. Copy that shape: current -> ref -> gate -> names, and `[]` when the gate is not ok.

DEFECT 1 DISSOLVES ONCE THE DESIGN IS RIGHT, AND THAT IS WORTH STATING RATHER THAN PATCHING. The worker reported a second transcriber - daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts:235 pins `repository.bootstrap` with `payloadKeys: ["dir","github","productName","profileVersion"]`, beside the registry test roster - and asked for it as a seventh owned path. It is a real second transcriber (its own comment calls that roster "a whole-tree census" and explains a missing row hides a served kind from every sweep in the file). BUT IT ONLY MOVES IF A COMMAND PAYLOAD KEY CHANGES, and under the corrected design none does: the names are READ SERVER-SIDE from the approved contract, never supplied by the operator's payload. `BootstrapRequest` is the internal request type, distinct from `PAYLOAD_KEYS`. So neither transcriber moves and this row touches neither roster - which also clears all four fileCollision warnings on this claim (task-537320ee, task-54b74b80, task-c422b106, task-dbc79d25 contend daemon-command-registry.test.ts and daemon-command-payload-keys.ts).
THE CONTRACT MUST BE THE AUTHORITY ANYWAY: a payload-supplied name list would let an operator write names the approved contract never required - the same class of defect as reading the unapproved revision.

TESTS 5C AND 6b ARE UNREACHABLE under real core admission, per the worker's measurement - dropped rather than carried as arms nobody can satisfy.

THERE IS NO `repository-bootstrap-command.test.ts`; the registered command is exercised through `repository-bootstrap-journey.test.ts`, which is where the real-command arms belong. Siblings: repository-bootstrap-{service,ports,read}.test.ts and repository-bootstrap-disclosure.test.ts.

[]`; controlled-profile-root-templates.ts:170 `envExample` de-duplicates through a Set and filters with `isContractVariableName`. `BootstrapRequest` (repository-bootstrap-contracts.ts:61-67) still has no names field, so the generator's `[]` default always wins and the real command emits a profile-only `.env.example`.
